articles.title: Fuel Stain Evap Ring
articles.summary: Faint ghost rings and solvent edge halos; fine ripple texture in clearcoat only. Practically invisible: a barely noticeable fine speckle in the highlight, nothing a viewer would call a stain.
articles.what: Fuel evaporated rings, ghost halos, and clean solvent edge marks. Up close: Very faint: sparse tiny slanted dashes, a few pixels long, scattered evenly like light rain streaks or specks. The ring and halo marks in the name do not show at this scale; the surface is otherwise smooth with soft mottling. From a distance: Practically invisible: a barely noticeable fine speckle in the highlight, nothing a viewer would call a stain. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Definitive Spec Replacements (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: fine.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Definitive Spec Replacements", or search for "Fuel Stain Evap Ring".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, fuel-door area and rear deck: where a spill would sit
Broad panels; too faint to matter on trim
No effect on legibility; numbers look clean.
Almost nothing: a few tiny glints in the highlight over smooth satin
Pairs well with: matte, satin, gloss.
pitfalls: Not a colour stain: it adds no colour, only micro shine variation
Not fuel rainbow film: no colour travel and no visible ring shapes at 1:1
Avoid: reads as dirt on light colours, too faint on matte.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.title: Add it as an overlay
examples.goal: Layer Fuel Stain Evap Ring over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.

articles.title: Hay Straw
articles.summary: Dry woven straw and hay-fiber strands with matte, fibrous sheen; MRC channels, micro texture. Reads as a smooth sheen with a sandy, slightly frosted shimmer; nothing straw-like survives.
articles.what: Dry woven straw and hay-fiber strands with a matte, fibrous sheen. Up close: Dense fine random speckle of bright dots one to three pixels wide, scattered like salt grains or powder; no straw strands, fibres or swirls are visible. Strong grainy glitter on metal inside the highlight, a light dusting on satin. From a distance: Reads as a smooth sheen with a sandy, slightly frosted shimmer; nothing straw-like survives. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Definitive Spec Replacements (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Definitive Spec Replacements", or search for "Hay Straw".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Whole body: even fine grain works on any panel
Metallic bases: where the glitter reads best
Numbers keep their colour; fine grain does not hurt legibility.
Light dusting of bright grains in the highlight; a soft sandy satin
Pairs well with: matte, satin, gloss.
pitfalls: Not straw or hay strands: the render shows random grain, no fibres
Not a colour: it adds no colour, only micro sparkle
Avoid: may look out of place on race cars, low contrast on light bases.
